responsibility: Implements rustc’s trait-selection and trait-solving layer: this crate is responsible for turning trait-, projection-, and type-relation questions into executable compiler logic, integrating inference, canonical queries, diagnostics, and supporting operations used throughout type checking, borrow checking, coherence, and code generation. Its crate root (`lib.rs`) defines the top-level organization and configuration of the subsystem, exposing the main solver, inference, region, and diagnostic components and loading crate-wide fluent messages. The `traits` module is the core execution engine for the trait system: it provides the trait APIs and query providers; performs obligation selection, projection, evaluation, and fulfillment using both the legacy and newer solver paths; supports codegen-time selection, coherence and specialization overlap checks, object safety, well-formedness, implied outlives, drop checking, const-evaluatability, structural-match and builtin-marker checks, auto-trait synthesis, canonical trait queries, MIR/NLL type operations, inference-relationship tracking, utilities, and the main trait diagnostic stack. The `autoderef.rs` root file contributes trait-aware autodereferencing, walking built-in and overloaded `Deref` steps, collecting the obligations required for overloaded dereferences, exposing the resulting deref chain to consumers such as method lookup and type operations, and detecting recursion-limit failures during the search. The `infer.rs` root file ties the crate into `rustc_infer` by extending inference contexts with trait-selection-specific helpers for equality and predicate checking, shallow and full implementation tests via selection and fulfillment, and execution of canonicalized trait queries with appropriately packaged responses. The `errors.rs` root file supplies the shared structured diagnostics, subdiagnostics, region/lifetime explanations, trait/impl conflict and closure/projection error payloads, and multipart suggestion builders used across the crate. Together, these pieces make `rustc_trait_selection` the compiler component that answers trait-system questions, propagates the resulting obligations through inference and query interfaces, performs trait-aware type operations like autoderef, and reports trait-related failures with structured diagnostics.
